title: PR threaded refactor journal and micro-invariant checklist
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal ledger for the multi-PR refactor I’m threading through inference routing and the KV cache codepaths. Not a final doc — mixture of TODOs, heuristics, small experiments to run, and notes to reviewers when I open the next follow-up PR(s).

High-level goal:
- Split routing decision logic away from RouteHandler into a smaller, testable Router service (inference/router) so we can:
  * isolate fallbacks
  * unit test routing table updates without spinning GPUs
  * enable canary route overrides in the console layer

Constraints / invariants to preserve (micro-invariants):
1) Backward binary compatibility for request proto: any new Router config must accept legacy fields and map them to the new enum.
2) Telemetry continuity: existing metrics (route.latency_{p50,p95}, route.fallback_count) must keep their names/labels.
3) Safe rollout: when Router returns error or timeout, behavior must remain exactly as today (fallback to compatible-hosted-model variant) — not intermediate failure.
4) KV-cache semantics: cache key format must not change for existing saved prefixes. If necessary, introduce a v2 prefix namespace rather than mutate v1.

Notes to self / rough plan of PRs (threaded):
- PR A (small): introduce interface IRouter in inference/router with no logic; wire minimal delegation from RouteHandler. Add unit tests for interface. (goal: low-risk, compile-only + tests)
- PR B (follow): implement simple config-led Router that reads from in-memory config and uses the existing logic. Add adapter for legacy config. (goal: keep runtime behavior identical)
- PR C (opt): replace heavy routing branches with decision table; add end-to-end smoke tests in CI that assert fallback counts identical for sampled traces.
- PR D (console): add canary override + rollout flag in Console (separate repo) that toggles Router.useNewTable; e2e with no GPUs via emulation.

Review checklist (what I want reviewers to focus on):
- Correctness: Do unit tests cover both legacy and new code paths? Edge cases for partial configs?
- Observability: Any changes to tags/labels/metric names? If yes, add migration mapping.
- Performance: PR B should not introduce extra allocations on hot path. Look for hidden string copies/formatting.
- Error handling: Confirm that any Router thrown exception is caught by RouteHandler and triggers previous fallback logic.
- KV cache keys: spot-check serialized key shapes in tests (binary diff against fixture).

Quick test ideas / scripts to run locally (commands I’ll paste in PRs):
- ./dev/run_router_unit_tests.sh --watch
- python infra/tools/trace_sampler.py --project inference --sample 1000 --compare-fallbacks prA-vs-current.json
- small perf harness: go run ./cmd/bench_router -concurrency 200 -seqlen 1024

Open questions / things to resolve before merging PR B:
- Do we need a config migration job for long-running Router instances? (follow-up: schedule rolling restart with graceful config reload)
- How to expose a safe toggle in the Console without creating accidental production rollouts? (ask product)
- Are there any downstream systems (billing pipeline, cost estimator) that parse the route.* metric format? I suspect yes; ask SRE/observability.

Risk matrix (quick):
- High: KV key mutation -> invalidates cache -> expensive cold-starts for customers. Mitigation: v2 namespace + migration plan + feature gate.
- Medium: Metric name changes causing dashboard noise/alerts. Mitigation: keep shim that emits old metric names for 30 days post-release.
- Low: Slight perf regression due to indirection. Mitigation: microbenchmarks + revert plan if >2% regression in p95.

Post-merge follow-ups (to capture):
- Sweep telemetry to annotate old dashboards (obs ticket).
- Add regression alert tied to fallback_count spike for routes modified by PR set.
- Add short doc (docs/route-migration.md) with config examples and troubleshooting steps.

Draft of the PR description headline (short):
Refactor: extract Router interface + config adapter to enable canary routing and safer rollouts

Draft description body (notes for PR A):
- Introduces IRouter interface and a very small adaptor that delegates to existing RouteHandler logic. No runtime behavioral change.
- Adds unit tests for adapter and interface invariants.
- This is the low-risk precursor to a larger decision-table implementation.

Reviewer checklist (to paste in PR template):
- [ ] Does CI unit test coverage look reasonable?
- [ ] Are there new allocations on the hot path (flagged by go test -bench)?
- [ ] Any new metric name / label changes documented?
- [ ] Integration test: smoke route fallbacks unchanged for 100 sampled traces.
- [ ] Docs: short migration note added for operator.

Mini-todo list (my brain dump):
- [ ] Write interface file and minimal tests (PR A)
- [ ] Add config adapter + legacy-mapping tests (PR B)
- [ ] Run bench harness and capture baseline (before PR B)
- [ ] Leave TODO TODO comments where a future optimization can safely be inserted
- [ ] Ping Maya + Rina for early review on PR B (they know the telemetry plumbing)

Snippets / helper text I keep copying into PR descriptions:
- Why we’re doing it: decoupling makes the routing logic easier to unit test and reason about, enabling safer canary and A/B experiments without heavy infra changes.
- Rollback plan: small PR A is safe to revert; PR B will include a feature flag so we can flip back to legacy behavior instantly.

Personal notes (scratch):
- Keep the Router interface very small: decide(request) -> RouteDecision + explanation. Avoid returning raw HTTP responses.
- Inline docstring for decision struct: include reason code and fallback hint for downstream logging.
- Consider adding a trace id to Router decisions for easier correlation with logs/metrics.

End-of-day quick status (for myself):
- Today: finished IRouter sketch + local compile, unit test skeletons pass.
- Tomorrow: flesh out legacy adapter and add the first integration smoke that asserts fallback parity with production traces.

Random links/refs I keep going back to:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood-inference.internal/display/INF/Route+Fallbacks
- Slack thread: slack://channel/eng-serving-runtime/thread/17382
- PR that broke metric naming earlier: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-inference/pull/3910

Notes to reviewers in-line when I open PR B:
- If you see a test that feels brittle, call it out — I want to keep the adapter tests stable across infra changes.
- If you suspect a metrics consumer will break, add the owner to the PR review or link a migration short-term.

-- Kellan
